source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew verse numbering align throughout Genesis 46–50.

key_decisions.decision: Preserves the request’s resident-foreigner status, the pasture crisis, and the permission sought, rather than implying citizenship or effortless relocation.
Keeps the exact age, Jacob’s negative assessment, and repeated sojourning framework without turning it into an objective claim that his life was short.
Retains the unusual little-ones basis of the provision instead of silently replacing it with a total household census.
Retains the desperate proposal of purchase and enslavement, the land’s personification, and both life/death and cultivation/desolation contrasts.
Follows the pinned Masoretic reading moved-to-cities; records the important enslaved-them variant in a note rather than silently importing it.
Retains the institutional exemption and its economic reason without supplying a moral evaluation.
Keeps Joseph’s explicit purchase of people as well as land, followed by seed provision, without euphemizing slavery as employment.
Retains gratitude and slavery in the same reply; does not turn the population’s speech into the narrator’s approval of the system.
Preserves the bodily oath gesture and kindness/faithfulness pair; records its connection with the earlier Abraham oath without replacing it with a modern gesture.
Retains lying-with-ancestors death imagery, removal from Egypt, and burial location while naming Joseph’s reply.
Follows the pinned bed vocalization; notes staff in the Greek tradition without changing the main text or inventing the object of the bow.
